transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that my body just feels... out of my control. 

At first, I was pacing around the apartment all night, just constantly moving and making all these notes for a supper club. But lately, I'm just so slowed down. My sister actually pointed it out—she says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on now. I just can't seem to move right.
During that time when you were pacing and making notes for the supper club, did you feel unusually euphoric, energized, or like you didn't need much sleep?

Yeah, I did. Um, it actually started right after I got fired from my job waiting tables. Instead of being upset about it, I just felt weirdly unstoppable and... really excited. So yeah, definitely energized. 

But at the same time, if anyone questioned my plans or told me I needed to slow down, I would just blow up at them. It felt like they were trying to ruin my life.
During the period where you felt slowed down, did you experience feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

Um, no, not really. I didn't feel guilty about anything, and I wouldn't say I felt worthless. It was... it was really just that physical heaviness I was talking about. Like, I just couldn't get my body to move normally, but I wasn't beating myself up in my head or anything like that.
During the time you've felt this physical heaviness, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I don't want to die or anything. It's really just... like I said, it's just the physical part. I still want to do things, I just feel like my body won't cooperate right now.

During that time when you felt unstoppable and were making all those notes, did you ever experience anything that didn't seem real to others, or hold beliefs that other people found impossible or strange?

No, I didn't have anything like that. Um, I mean, people thought my plans for the supper club were a bit much, or maybe too ambitious since I'd just lost my job waiting tables, but I didn't believe anything impossible. And I definitely wasn't seeing or hearing things that weren't there, if that's what you mean. I just... I just felt really confident that my idea was going to work out, and it made sense to me at the time.
During that time when you felt unstoppable and were working on your supper club plans, how many days in a row did that feeling of high energy and activity last?

Um, I'm not really sure exactly how many days it was. It's hard to put an exact number on it. It just felt like a continuous stretch of time where I was going non-stop. I didn't really keep track of the days while it was happening.
Looking back, do you think that period where you were going non-stop lasted for at least a full week, or was it shorter than that?

I really don't know if it was a full week. Um, it could have been, but it might have been a few days less. Like I said, I wasn't really paying attention to the calendar when I was in the middle of it all.

During that period where you were going non-stop, did your behavior cause significant problems at work or in your relationships, such as getting into trouble or causing people to be genuinely worried about you?

Yeah, it definitely caused problems. I mean... I haven't been able to hold together my work plans at all, or even my rent arrangements. My family commitments just kind of fell apart, too. People were definitely worried about me. It actually got to the point where my sister had to take me to the crisis clinic, because I just... I couldn't get basic responsibilities organized on my own anymore.
When your sister took you to the crisis clinic, was it because you were a danger to yourself or others, or was it because you were unable to care for your basic needs?

I'm not really sure. I don't think I was going to hurt myself or anyone else, if that's what you mean. It was mostly just... well, like I said, I couldn't figure out how to pay my rent or keep my work schedule straight anymore. I guess I just couldn't handle my normal day-to-day stuff, and she saw that, so she just told me we were going. I don't know exactly what she told the people at the clinic.
When your sister took you to the crisis clinic, were you admitted to the hospital for any period of time?
No, I wasn't admitted. They just talked to me for a while and then sent me home with my sister.
Have you ever had any other periods in your life, besides this one, where you felt that same high energy, lack of need for sleep, and feeling unstoppable?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think so. This is the first time anything like this has ever happened to me. I've never felt that kind of... unstoppable energy before, or gone without sleep like that.
Looking back over the last two years or more, have you felt down, sad, or low in your mood for most of the time, even when you aren't feeling this physical heaviness?

No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't really felt sad or down for most of the time over the last couple of years. I mean, before all this started, my mood was just... normal, I guess. I definitely haven't felt low like that constantly.
